When an introductory subordinate clause precedes the main clause, a comma is common, particularly if it prevents a misreading. Short introductory adjuncts sometimes appear without one, depending on house style and clarity. Commas around a supplementary relative clause are normally paired when the main clause continues: The director, who had just arrived, opened the meeting. A defining relative identifying the intended member ordinarily has no such commas. Punctuation can therefore change reference, not merely rhythm. Do not separate a subject from its verb simply because the subject is long; internal commas may still enclose a parenthetical within that subject. The board, after a long discussion, approved the proposal has two commas performing that enclosing job. A comma before a coordinator may be omitted in short clear clauses or added to prevent confusion. A punctuation judgement must specify genre and intended analysis. Published literary prose sometimes uses deliberate fragments or comma splices for an identifiable effect; this does not make them a safe default for a formal answer. Conversely, a stylistic comma is not automatically an error. In cumulative editing, first identify every clause and the relation between clauses, then examine marks. A semicolon cannot turn a subordinate fragment into an independent clause. Because the lift was broken; we took the stairs remains faulty for the intended reason relationship. Write Because the lift was broken, we took the stairs instead. independent clause ; independent clause Links two complete, closely related statements. introductory subordinate clause , main clause A common clear boundary; short clauses allow some convention-dependent flexibility. The results arrived. We checked the totals. Two full stops separate complete statements. The results arrived, but the annex was missing. But coordinates two clauses and expresses contrast. The teams came from Multan, Punjab; Sukkur, Sindh; and Quetta, Balochistan. Semicolons clarify complex list items containing internal commas. The volunteers who had registered received badges. The volunteers, who had registered, received badges. Both are grammatical. The first identifies a subset; the second presents registration as supplementary information about the contextually identified volunteers. A short opening phrase may appear without a comma: In June we moved. Add one when it aids interpretation; do not declare one version universally ungrammatical. The road was flooded, the bus turned back. The road was flooded, so the bus turned back. So explicitly presents a result; a full stop or semicolon can avoid adding a causal claim if none is intended. The documents on the highest shelf, were damaged. The documents on the highest shelf were damaged. The comma wrongly separates the complete subject from its predicate. comma splice Two independent clauses joined by a comma alone in a context requiring a stronger boundary. The alarm rang, we left. supplementary relative A relative clause adding a separate comment about an identified referent. Mina, who lives nearby, helped. source-93f2b5c2495752 source-2ce8f4ad32dfe5 source-c9f14a7debeeb5

concepts.title: Colons, apostrophes and compact written forms
concepts.definition: A colon introduces an explanation, elaboration, list or quotation within an appropriate written structure. An apostrophe marks certain possessive and omitted-letter forms; it is not a general mark of plurality.

glossary.definition: A grammatical construction often marked by ’s or s’, expressing a relationship.
glossary.example: the school’s entrance

glossary.definition: An abbreviation pronounced as individual letters.
glossary.example: NGO

concepts.searchText: gv5-d24-m02 Colons, apostrophes and compact written forms O P gv5-topic-d24-c02 gv5-topic-d24-c08 A colon introduces an explanation, elaboration, list or quotation within an appropriate written structure. An apostrophe marks certain possessive and omitted-letter forms; it is not a general mark of plurality. A colon often follows a complete introductory clause: We need three items: a torch, a map and a whistle. Avoid separating an ordinary verb from its required object just to announce a list: The items include: a torch is unnecessary punctuation in continuous prose. Write The items include a torch, a map and a whistle. After the colon, material can be a phrase rather than a full clause. The punctuation signals how that material elaborates the introduction, so a colon differs from a semicolon joining independent clauses. For a singular possessive, a common convention adds apostrophe-s: the writer’s desk. Regular plural possessives ending in s place the apostrophe after that ending: the writers’ desks. Irregular plurals take apostrophe-s: the children’s drawings. Its is possessive without an apostrophe, while it’s contracts it is or it has. Ordinary plurals and dates take no apostrophe: five MPs, the 1990s. Some style guides use apostrophes for single-letter plurals such as dot your i’s; that special convention does not justify writing three file’s. Joint and separate relationships need meaning rather than an automatic last-name rule. Ana and Omar’s shared flat presents one jointly held flat; Ana’s and Omar’s separate flats explicitly mark two relationships. Awkward expressions can be recast as the flat shared by Ana and Omar. Singular names ending in s admit house-style variation: James’s notebook and James’ notebook both occur in established editorial systems. Possessive relationships are broader than ownership, as in yesterday’s meeting. Contractions such as don’t and we’ve are grammatical; a formal assignment may prefer uncontracted forms without turning contractions into errors. Numerals, initials and abbreviations also involve convention. A publication may choose 8 October 2026 or October 8, 2026; apply one consistent system and avoid ambiguous numerical dates where readers use different orders. Dr and Dr. belong to different punctuation conventions, not different standards of intelligence. Introduce an unfamiliar initialism in full before relying on it. The plural normally adds s, while a possessive adds the relevant apostrophe: two NGOs and an NGO’s report. Decimal separators, units and percentage spacing can depend on disciplinary style; preserve a source’s numerical meaning when changing its presentation. complete introduction : elaboration The second unit expands or specifies the first. regular plural ending in -s + apostrophe Marks a possessive relationship involving a regular plural noun. One difficulty remained: the missing signature. The noun phrase after the colon explains the difficulty. The teachers’ comments were attached to the children’s work. Teachers is regular plural; children is an irregular plural. It’s evident that the NGO has changed its timetable. It’s expands to it is, while its is possessive. James’s article was published. James’ article was published. Both possessive spellings are established under different style conventions; choose the stipulated system. Apostrophes in single-letter plurals are allowed by some styles for clarity. Treat that as a limited editorial convention, not a rule for every plural. The three NGO’s submitted report’s. The three NGOs submitted reports. These are ordinary plurals, not possessives. Its clear that the device has lost it’s settings. It’s clear that the device has lost its settings. The first expression means it is; the second is possessive. genitive A grammatical construction often marked by ’s or s’, expressing a relationship. the school’s entrance initialism An abbreviation pronounced as individual letters. NGO source-93f2b5c2495752 source-8cf60a1688508e source-fb41efc1d03fc7 source-b5b38b055ab426 source-bb04455ae3afd3

concepts.title: Quotation, interruption and sentence-final marks
concepts.definition: Quotation marks identify quoted wording or another explicitly defined editorial use. Parentheses, brackets, dashes, hyphens and ellipses do different jobs; none is a general substitute for any inconvenient punctuation.

glossary.definition: Dots indicating an omission or an appropriate trailing-off effect.
glossary.example: The document states that “the fee … is refundable”.

glossary.definition: A mark joining elements within some compound expressions.
glossary.example: a two-day workshop

concepts.searchText: gv5-d24-m03 Quotation, interruption and sentence-final marks O P gv5-topic-d24-c03 gv5-topic-d24-c04 gv5-topic-d24-c05 Quotation marks identify quoted wording or another explicitly defined editorial use. Parentheses, brackets, dashes, hyphens and ellipses do different jobs; none is a general substitute for any inconvenient punctuation. A direct question normally ends with a question mark: Has the office reopened? An indirect report normally ends with the mark appropriate to the whole sentence: She asked whether the office had reopened. Do you know whether it has reopened? is itself a question and takes a question mark. An exclamation mark signals an exclamatory expression or emphatic utterance. Multiple exclamation marks occur in informal messages, but restrained formal writing normally avoids them. That preference concerns register; it is not evidence that informal messages must obey a ban on repeated marks. Single or double outer quotation marks can both be used under established styles. When a quotation contains another quotation, switch the inner pair to distinguish levels. Punctuation placement depends partly on whether a mark belongs to the quoted words and partly on the chosen convention. British logical placement and common American practice differ for commas and full stops. Question marks should reflect the intended question: Did she say “Leave now”? asks about the saying; She asked, “May I leave?” quotes a question. Do not add a second full stop mechanically after the closing quotation. Round parentheses enclose an aside; square brackets in a quotation commonly identify editorial additions or clarifications. The brackets must not make an uncertain interpretation look like the speaker’s original wording. Dashes can mark interruption, amplification or a strongly separated parenthesis. A hyphen joins elements within some compounds: a three-year project. It is shorter and has a different function from a dash. The need for hyphens varies by position and convention: a well-known author but the author is well known. An -ly adverb normally does not need a hyphen in a clearly written modifier such as a carefully planned route. An ellipsis can mark an omission from quoted text or a trailing-off effect in an appropriate genre. Omitting words must not change the represented claim. Removing not from a quotation is a substantive distortion even if an ellipsis is printed. A complete omitted sentence and an omitted phrase may be punctuated differently by different style guides; consult the specified guide for the number and spacing of dots. Parenthetical material inside a sentence normally leaves the main sentence’s ending outside the closing parenthesis; a complete independent parenthetical sentence may retain its own final mark inside. Analyse the enclosing structure before choosing the position. outer quotation + contrasting inner quotation Keeps nested quoted material distinguishable. number + unit singular + noun, with a hyphenated modifier A common pattern: a ten-minute break; compare the break lasted ten minutes. She asked, “Is the archive open?” The question mark belongs to the quoted question. The archive closes at six (except on Fridays). The parenthesis sits inside the sentence; its full stop follows the closing parenthesis. The report described a carefully planned, three-stage operation. The -ly modifier has no hyphen; three-stage is a compound premodifier. Did he say “The door is locked”? He asked, “Is the door locked?” The first is an outer question about a statement; the second quotes a question. The question mark follows the relevant structure. Some familiar compounds keep a dictionary hyphen even in positions where other compounds open up. Check a reliable dictionary and the required house style rather than inventing a universal positional rule. She asked whether the office was open? She asked whether the office was open. The whole construction is a statement reporting a question. It was a five years plan. It was a five-year plan. In the compound premodifier, the unit year is singular; a hyphen clarifies the relationship. ellipsis mark Dots indicating an omission or an appropriate trailing-off effect. The document states that “the fee … is refundable”. hyphen A mark joining elements within some compound expressions. a two-day workshop source-93f2b5c2495752 source-89176b529bbc02 source-c9f14a7debeeb5

concepts.title: Capitalisation, spelling and editorial consistency
concepts.definition: Orthography is the system of written forms, including spelling, capitalisation and word division. Some orthographic choices distinguish words; others vary legitimately between national and editorial conventions.

glossary.definition: The conventional written representation of a language.
glossary.example: spelling and capitalisation

glossary.definition: A publication’s chosen conventions among available forms.
glossary.example: a policy of sentence-case headings

concepts.searchText: gv5-d24-m04 Capitalisation, spelling and editorial consistency O P gv5-topic-d24-c07 gv5-topic-d24-c09 Orthography is the system of written forms, including spelling, capitalisation and word division. Some orthographic choices distinguish words; others vary legitimately between national and editorial conventions. Capitalise the first word of a normal written sentence, the pronoun I and proper names: Zainab, Pakistan, Urdu and October. A common noun does not become a proper noun merely because it is important: the committee announced the decision is a normal general description. A particular organisation’s official name can require capitals: the National Library. Titles before personal names often receive capitals, while general references often remain lower case. Check whether the wording is an official name, a descriptive phrase or a house-style abbreviation before changing its capitals. British and American spelling conventions differ in words such as colour/color, centre/center and travelled/traveled. Both standard systems are legitimate; this course uses British defaults and identifies American alternatives. British publishing itself permits more than one convention for some words, including forms in -ise and -ize. Do not label every -ize spelling American. Programme is a common British form for a plan or broadcast, while program is standard in computing. A consistent editing policy should still allow quoted material, names and technical forms to retain their authentic spelling. Capitalisation of headings and titles varies between sentence case and title case. A sentence-case heading need not capitalise every major word. Institutions and legal publications may prescribe forms such as Section 12, while another style uses section 12 in running prose. Names of languages keep capitals; ordinary names of academic fields often do not unless they form part of an official course title. Compound words may be open, closed or hyphenated, and usage changes over time: a dictionary entry and a publication’s stated style are better evidence than a remembered universal rule. Separate error correction from editorial normalisation. Writing enviroment for environment is a spelling error; writing organization in a British document may match an established British house style. A question that asks for one correct spelling must avoid offering two standard variants unless it states the convention being tested. Numerical forms also need a stated purpose: scientific prose, dates, tables and literary prose often use different presentation rules. In your final editing pass, check the chosen system, official names, consistency and meaning. Do not remove capitals, hyphens or abbreviations blindly from specialist material merely because the general default differs. proper name → capitalisation appropriate to the name Distinguishes an identified name from a general description. house style + dictionary evidence Resolves legitimate variants without inventing grammatical prohibitions. The department offers courses in chemistry and English. English names a language; chemistry is a general field name here. The colour of the laboratory’s sign has changed. Colour follows the course’s British editorial default. The software program supports the festival programme. The two forms can coexist under a normal British computing/general distinction. The centre has reopened. The center has reopened. Both are standard; the first matches the course’s British spelling default. Official names, quotations and stipulated specialist notation can retain a different convention within an otherwise consistent document. The committee met on monday to discuss urdu teaching. The committee met on Monday to discuss Urdu teaching. The day and language names need capitals. The enviroment report was published. The environment report was published. Environment requires the internal n; this is a spelling correction rather than a national variant. orthography The conventional written representation of a language. spelling and capitalisation house style A publication’s chosen conventions among available forms. a policy of sentence-case headings source-93f2b5c2495752 source-8cf60a1688508e source-bd36d7502df16b source-bb04455ae3afd3

concepts.title: Confusable words: meaning before substitution
concepts.definition: Confusable words are expressions whose spelling, sound or associated meaning makes them easy to interchange. A reliable choice depends on sense, grammatical pattern and context; a simple noun-versus-verb shortcut is sometimes useful but not exhaustive.

glossary.definition: A conventional association of words in a particular sense or pattern.
glossary.example: reach a conclusion

glossary.definition: A particular meaning of a word in context.
glossary.example: effect meaning bring about

concepts.searchText: gv5-d25-m01 Confusable words: meaning before substitution G L P Q gv5-topic-d25-c01 Confusable words are expressions whose spelling, sound or associated meaning makes them easy to interchange. A reliable choice depends on sense, grammatical pattern and context; a simple noun-versus-verb shortcut is sometimes useful but not exhaustive. Learn a contrast inside a meaningful sentence. Advice is normally the noun for a recommendation; advise is the related verb: Your advice helped; please advise me. Lose means fail to retain or win, whereas loose commonly means not firmly attached: Do not lose the loose screw. Principal can mean main or the head of an institution; principle names a rule or belief. A spelling resemblance does not make two words interchangeable. Identify the intended message first, then choose the form and the complement pattern that expresses it. Affect is commonly a verb meaning influence, while effect commonly names a result. Those common patterns do not exhaust either word. Effect can be a verb meaning bring about: The agreement effected a change. Affect also has a specialised noun sense in psychology. Judicial concerns courts or judges; judicious means showing sound judgement. A judge’s decision can therefore be judicial even if it is unwise, and a judicious decision need not come from a court. Questions must provide enough context to distinguish the intended senses rather than pretend one adjective is always the better choice. Other useful contrasts include complement, which completes or fits something, and compliment, which expresses praise; imply, which presents an indirect suggestion, and infer, which draws a conclusion from evidence. Economic concerns an economy; economical describes sparing use of resources. Farther and further overlap in distance uses, while further also clearly means additional. Continual often highlights repetition and continuous an unbroken process, but contexts and established senses overlap. Do not turn a useful tendency into an absolute rule when a reliable dictionary records a broader range. Lexical diagnosis differs from proving a syntactic error. An unusual but meaningful word may be grammatical; a near-synonym can make a false or inappropriate claim without breaking syntax. Evaluate three questions separately: Is the form possible? Does it express the intended sense? Does it suit the register? In an objective item, the supplied definition or situation should eliminate alternative senses. In original writing, explain a proposed replacement. Replacing judicial with judicious merely because the latter sounds approving can change a legal classification into an evaluation; that is not a meaning-preserving correction. advise + person + to-infinitive A common advice-giving verb pattern. effect + noun phrase The verb can mean bring about, as in effect a change. The adviser offered practical advice. The person noun and uncountable advice belong to different patterns. The reforms affected prices, but their effects differed across districts. Affected means influenced; effects names results. The mediator effected an agreement after a judicious intervention. Effected means brought about; judicious evaluates judgement rather than identifying a court function. The panel reviewed a judicial decision. The panel reviewed a judicious decision. Both are grammatical but different: the first identifies a court-related decision, the second evaluates its wisdom. Effect is not restricted to noun use: To effect a repair means to bring it about. Affect has a specialised noun use; use a dictionary to identify its disciplinary sense. Please advice the visitors to retain their tickets. Please advise the visitors to retain their tickets. The imperative requires the verb advise. The new rules will effect the daily routine, meaning influence it. The new rules will affect the daily routine. For the specified influence meaning, affect is the appropriate verb; effect would require a bring-about interpretation. collocation A conventional association of words in a particular sense or pattern. reach a conclusion lexical sense A particular meaning of a word in context. effect meaning bring about source-d1c9bd91ec669b source-c8a280ba934bd7 source-f3988fbed0a134 source-de295c8f9dba2d

concepts.title: Lexical patterns and preposition choices
concepts.definition: Lexical grammar concerns the grammatical patterns selected by particular words and senses. A preposition may be required in one pattern while a different construction uses no preposition or a different complement.

glossary.definition: The patterns of complements selected by a word.
glossary.example: insist on checking; insist that we check

glossary.definition: A limit associated with a particular word or sense.
glossary.example: capable of doing, not capable to do in this pattern

concepts.searchText: gv5-d25-m02 Lexical patterns and preposition choices G L P Q gv5-topic-d25-c02 gv5-topic-d25-c03 Lexical grammar concerns the grammatical patterns selected by particular words and senses. A preposition may be required in one pattern while a different construction uses no preposition or a different complement. Compare discuss the proposal with a discussion about the proposal. The verb discuss ordinarily takes its topic as a direct object; the related noun discussion has other complement patterns. Learn words with example frames instead of memorising a single preposition beside an isolated dictionary form. Depend on the result is one common pattern, but depend can also occur without an expressed complement when the context supplies it. An incomplete classroom rule such as every verb must take its memorised preposition can therefore create mistakes. Insist illustrates why a lexical pattern is not an absolute following-word rule. A speaker can insist on a receipt, insist on checking the figures, insist that the bill is wrong, or insist that the figures be checked. The choice affects form and sometimes meaning: insisting that a claim is true asserts it firmly, whereas insisting that an action be done demands that action. Capable of handling the task contrasts with able to handle the task. Similar meanings do not license the same complementation after every adjective. Prepositions can also change a relationship rather than merely distinguish right from wrong. An increase in prices identifies what increases; an increase of ten per cent measures its amount. Inform someone of a decision and inform someone about a new service are both established patterns. Between and among depend on the relationship being expressed; between can identify distinct relationships involving more than two participants, so the number of names alone does not settle every case. Check a dictionary’s sense and examples, especially when a purported correction declares an unfamiliar combination impossible. Many restrictions belong to a particular sense, construction or register. Compare consist of with be composed of; active comprise and passive be comprised of are established, although some editorial traditions prefer alternatives. A teacher can recommend comprises for economy without marking every comprised of as a grammatical error. Identify whether the problem is a missing complement, an incompatible form or a stylistic preference. When several constructions express the same message, preserve the intended participants, direction and scope. Replacing a preposition mechanically may change the relationship even if the result remains grammatical. insist on + noun/-ing A demand or firm requirement focused through on. insist (that) + finite clause A firmly asserted proposition or a demanded action, depending on clause form and context. We discussed the revised timetable. Discuss takes its topic as a direct object here. The guide informed us about the new entrance and of the revised fee. Both information patterns can be valid; neither preposition is universally forbidden. She insisted that the committee should reconsider the evidence. A standard British mandative pattern uses should in a that-clause. An increase in rent was announced. An increase of five per cent was announced. Both are grammatical: in identifies the changing variable; of identifies the size of the increase. A common pairing does not exclude other clause patterns: insist on a receipt and insist that a receipt be issued are both standard. We discussed about the timetable. We discussed the timetable. For the intended ordinary transitive topic pattern, discuss takes a direct object. She is capable to prepare the accounts. She is capable of preparing the accounts. Capable selects of + noun/-ing in this pattern; able to prepare is a valid alternative. complementation The patterns of complements selected by a word. insist on checking; insist that we check lexical restriction A limit associated with a particular word or sense. capable of doing, not capable to do in this pattern source-9ed1c4e8bff777 source-f19b5fb022dfc1 source-624ab6294e2bb8 source-3d6f341171cc0f source-3584b7a9f9bc59 source-a62dca14faa64b

concepts.title: Countability, agreement and national alternatives
concepts.definition: Countability and agreement are grammatical choices associated with a noun’s sense and the construction in which it occurs. National conventions can favour different choices without making all alternatives errors.

glossary.definition: Agreement influenced by interpreted meaning rather than form alone.
glossary.example: The team are arguing among themselves.

glossary.definition: A noun used without ordinary individual counting in a particular sense.
glossary.example: some equipment

concepts.searchText: gv5-d25-m03 Countability, agreement and national alternatives G L P Q gv5-topic-d25-c04 gv5-topic-d25-c06 Countability and agreement are grammatical choices associated with a noun’s sense and the construction in which it occurs. National conventions can favour different choices without making all alternatives errors. In ordinary general English, information, advice, furniture and equipment are uncountable. Write some information or two pieces of information, not two informations for that intended sense. The restriction belongs to English usage, not to whether the real-world objects can be counted. A piece, item, study or other appropriate unit can express an individual instance. Other nouns change their countability with meaning: paper can be a material, while a paper can be an article or examination. Learn the intended sense and a natural counting expression together. Research is normally uncountable for an activity or body of investigation: extensive research. Plural researches is also established, especially when separate investigations are in view, but it is less frequent and is not an ordinary substitute for studies in every context. A standard learner explanation should acknowledge such documented uses without encouraging an unnatural plural in every research context. Agreement also depends on analysis: the news is singular in standard use; the scissors are plural; a pair of scissors is singular because pair heads that noun phrase. A measurement can be treated as one amount: Ten kilometres is a long walk. Collective nouns such as committee can take singular unit agreement or plural member agreement in British English: The committee has issued its decision; The committee are divided in their opinions. American edited usage more often favours singular agreement for the unit. Consistency of reference is useful, but an overt switch to members can justify different number. Data admits plural and mass-noun agreement under established usage and disciplinary conventions. The data are incomplete and The data is incomplete therefore need a stated editorial context before a test can require one form exclusively. A national comparison must specify what varies. American English often permits a past simple with just, already or yet in contexts where a British default favours present perfect; it also has gotten in many get constructions. These are established alternatives, not automatic tense mistakes. Conversely, choosing a national label cannot justify a malformed auxiliary sequence such as has went. Fewer is a common edited choice for individually counted plural items; less is standard with measurements and amounts, as in less than ten miles. The rule concerns how the quantity is construed, not just the visible plural ending. uncountable noun → quantity expression + of + noun Expresses separate units without inventing an ordinary plural of the mass noun. collective unit/member interpretation → suitable agreement Regional convention and intended reference affect the available choices. The office bought three items of equipment. Items supplies the countable units; equipment remains uncountable. The committee are exchanging their individual views. British member-oriented agreement is appropriate in this context. Less than eight kilometres remains to be surveyed. Less than treats the distance as an amount; a plural unit word does not by itself require fewer. The data are available. The data is available. Both are established; discipline and house style can specify the preferred analysis. Plural researches is documented in particular contexts, but research is normally uncountable in ordinary academic statements. Do not treat a historical or specialist sense as the everyday default. They supplied several useful informations. They supplied several useful pieces of information. The intended ordinary information sense is uncountable. The news are encouraging. The news is encouraging. News has singular agreement in this ordinary standard construction. notional agreement Agreement influenced by interpreted meaning rather than form alone. The team are arguing among themselves. mass noun A noun used without ordinary individual counting in a particular sense. some equipment source-a95ed69b7ca939 source-5e8743788d0639 source-287989cd31ff3a source-24f0ac0bd69ddf source-d683fd9c85a960 source-090178afec1c2c source-8cf60a1688508e

concepts.title: Register, regional English and evidence-based editing
concepts.definition: Register is language choice associated with purpose, audience and situation. A form can be grammatical and standard in a regional variety while a different expression is clearer for an unfamiliar international audience.

glossary.definition: Differences in established use associated with geographical communities.
glossary.example: prepone in Indian English

glossary.definition: An edit made for purpose and audience rather than a universal grammar law.
glossary.example: bring forward for an unfamiliar audience

concepts.searchText: gv5-d25-m04 Register, regional English and evidence-based editing G L P Q gv5-topic-d25-c05 gv5-topic-d25-c07 gv5-topic-d25-c08 Register is language choice associated with purpose, audience and situation. A form can be grammatical and standard in a regional variety while a different expression is clearer for an unfamiliar international audience. Begin an edit by identifying the intended reader. A message to a friend, a laboratory report and an administrative request have different expectations. Formality does not require rare words, constant passive voice or avoidance of every contraction in every genre. A direct active sentence can be entirely formal: The committee rejected the bid. Neutral clear language is often the most effective default. If an assignment asks for a particular register, revise toward that register while distinguishing the preference from a claim of universal grammatical incorrectness. Some learners find English articles, countability, auxiliary patterns or prepositions difficult because their other languages organise these relationships differently. Urdu-speaking learners may recognise particular translation habits, but no individual’s error profile should be guessed from first-language identity. For example, practise He has a question rather than He has question, and Did she attend? rather than Did she attended? Explain the English pattern itself. Do not present every regional expression as evidence of deficient thought or assume that all learners share one background. Prepone is recorded in Indian English with the meaning move to an earlier time. For readers unfamiliar with it, bring forward the meeting can communicate more widely. That editorial decision does not prove prepone nonexistent. A request for someone’s good name may be a regional politeness formula; good name also has the established reputation sense in protect the organisation’s good name. Context therefore matters before a word pair is labelled wrong. Likewise, American insure can mean ensure; a British default may reserve insure mainly for insurance without declaring that broader American use invalid. Use a transparent editorial vocabulary. Ungrammatical for the intended standard pattern identifies a structural problem; unusual identifies frequency or idiomaticity; informal identifies register; regional identifies distribution; misleading identifies an interpretation problem. These labels can overlap, but none should stand in for evidence. If a sentence is already grammatical, say so and explain any optional revision. A source register should identify the authority and the sense actually checked. Newly authored practice should never claim to be an official past question or an examiner’s preference without authentic supporting records. purpose + audience + meaning → register choice Selects wording for the communicative situation without inventing a universal grammar ban. diagnosis label + evidence + optional alternative Makes editing reasoning explicit and reviewable. Please bring the appointment forward to Thursday. An internationally clear paraphrase of prepone in its recorded regional sense. The American guide advises readers to insure that the valve is closed. Insure can have a make-certain sense in established American use; ensure matches the course’s British default. The department’s good name depends on honest reporting. Good name has a standard reputation meaning and is not inherently faulty. The policy was rejected. The committee rejected the policy. Both are grammatical and can be formal. The active version identifies the actor; the passive may suit a different information focus. Regional labels describe use; they do not make every such form unsuitable in its own audience. A wider-audience alternative can be recommended explicitly as an editorial choice. Did she attended the seminar? Did she attend the seminar? Do-support carries the tense; the lexical verb has its base form. He has question about the procedure. He has a question about the procedure. Question is an ordinary singular countable noun in this intended sense and needs a determiner. regional variation Differences in established use associated with geographical communities. prepone in Indian English register-sensitive revision An edit made for purpose and audience rather than a universal grammar law. bring forward for an unfamiliar audience source-f7c1a80292d10b source-777ef904b95b58 source-b30c57ec4e32c9 source-8cf60a1688508e source-a95ed69b7ca939

concepts.title: Connecting sentences: cohesion, reference and recoverable omission
concepts.definition: Cohesion consists of visible grammatical and lexical links across a text. Coherence is the interpretable connection among its ideas; a text can contain many linking words and still lack a sensible argument.

glossary.definition: Linked expressions identifying a participant or topic.
glossary.example: a parcel → the parcel → it

glossary.definition: Omission whose grammatical content is recoverable.
glossary.example: I can attend; she cannot.

concepts.searchText: gv5-d26-m01 Connecting sentences: cohesion, reference and recoverable omission M N gv5-topic-d26-c01 gv5-topic-d26-c02 gv5-topic-d26-c03 Cohesion consists of visible grammatical and lexical links across a text. Coherence is the interpretable connection among its ideas; a text can contain many linking words and still lack a sensible argument. Read two sentences together before judging their connection. A pronoun can carry forward an established participant: A courier arrived. She carried a sealed envelope. Repeating courier is not an error, but she is economical when its reference is clear. This and that can also refer to a whole previous event: The envelope was empty. This caused concern. A summary noun, such as this omission, can identify the intended aspect more precisely. It is useful when several earlier facts could compete, not compulsory after every this. Build a reference chain by tracking a participant through noun phrases, pronouns and descriptions. A visitor, the visitor and she can form a chain. Do not vary technical labels just to avoid repeating a word: a permit, a licence and an authorisation may refer to different legal objects. Substitution replaces repeated material with a smaller expression: The red folder is damaged; use the blue one. Ellipsis leaves recoverable material unspoken: Mara can attend, but I cannot. The omitted content is attend, understood from the first clause. Omission has grammatical and interpretative limits. In The first room was warm; the second, cold, the missing was is recoverable in a coordinated comparison. In a detached formal sentence such as The second cold, it may instead look like a fragment. So can substitute for a proposition after suitable verbs: I think so. Do so commonly substitutes for an action: The clerk promised to check and did so. It is not interchangeable with it or one in every context. Choose the substitute by the size and kind of unit being replaced. Reference can point backwards, forwards or outside the text. The first is often called anaphora, the second cataphora and the third deixis. A pronoun need not replace a single noun: propositional this can refer to a preceding clause or stretch of discourse. However, an editor should test whether readers recover the intended content rather than merely any plausible content. Cohesion also includes lexical repetition and relations such as part–whole. These support interpretation but do not establish truth or logical consequence. A therefore between unrelated claims creates a misleading inference rather than coherence. established noun phrase → pronoun Maintains a participant when reference is identifiable. auxiliary + omitted verb phrase Avoids repeating material recoverable from context. A lamp failed. It was replaced immediately. It continues the lamp reference. The first proposal was costly; the second, affordable. Was is recoverable in the second coordinated unit. The supplier promised to replace the faulty part and did so. Did so substitutes for replacing the part, not for the supplier. The archive closed early. This disrupted the visit. The archive closed early. This closure disrupted the visit. Both grammatical; the summary noun makes the event reference explicit. Informal situational ellipsis such as Ready? is normal conversation, though a formal standalone report usually supplies the full clause. The clerk promised to inspect the meter and did one. The clerk promised to inspect the meter and did so. One substitutes for a suitable noun, not the inspection action. A researcher challenged a manager after she altered the figures. After the manager altered the figures, a researcher challenged her. If the manager altered them, repeating the role removes the competing she reference. reference chain Linked expressions identifying a participant or topic. a parcel → the parcel → it ellipsis Omission whose grammatical content is recoverable. I can attend; she cannot. source-2e5cd32b34733d source-028b7ffa729def

concepts.title: Time, topics and the movement of information
concepts.definition: Textual progression is the way a passage moves from established information to a developing point. Temporal consistency preserves intended time relationships, rather than requiring every verb to have one tense.

glossary.definition: Keeping a participant or issue traceable across sentences.
glossary.example: The lease expired. Its expiry ...

glossary.definition: Material assumed identifiable to the reader in context.
glossary.example: the workshop in the second sentence

concepts.searchText: gv5-d26-m02 Time, topics and the movement of information M N gv5-topic-d26-c04 gv5-topic-d26-c05 gv5-topic-d26-c06 Textual progression is the way a passage moves from established information to a developing point. Temporal consistency preserves intended time relationships, rather than requiring every verb to have one tense. A reader needs to know how the next sentence relates to the current one. A useful default is to begin from something already identifiable and then develop it: The school opened a workshop. The workshop offers evening classes. You can also repeat a subject deliberately to maintain a topic. Beginning with new information is legitimate when introducing a contrast or changing focus. The practical question is whether the sequence guides the intended reader, not whether every sentence follows one fixed template or starts with a different word. Transitions express relations such as addition, contrast, concession, consequence and example. They do not create those relations. The route was shorter; nevertheless, it took longer expresses an unexpected contrast. The route was shorter; therefore, it took longer would require extra circumstances to explain the result. Topic sentences often state a paragraph’s controlling idea, but can occur after an opening example or be implicit. A paragraph may contain several related claims serving one purpose. Organise supporting details so that the relationship among them remains visible. Tense choices can change purposefully within a paragraph. The clinic opened in 2018 and now treats patients daily contrasts a completed opening with an ongoing practice. A research summary may use the past for methods and the present for a still-relevant interpretation. A past perfect can place an event before the narrative reference point, after which ordinary past forms may continue the sequence. Voice also changes legitimately to maintain the topic: We received a damaged instrument. It was repaired the next day. The passive keeps the instrument in view. Theme and rheme are terms used in some linguistic frameworks for the point of departure of a clause and its development. Given and new describe information status, while topic and focus describe what is discussed and what is foregrounded. These distinctions overlap but are not identical. A passive, cleft or fronted phrase can organise information without altering the underlying event. Changes can nevertheless affect implication, contrast or presupposition. When revising an extended passage, compare its entire information route; a locally concise active sentence may break the established chain that a passive sentence maintained more effectively. past event + now + present situation Separates a completed event from a current state. claim + nevertheless + contrasting outcome Signals an outcome contrary to an expectation. The roof leaked last winter. It is secure now. A justified past-to-present shift distinguishes then from now. An old map was discovered. The map revealed a forgotten path. New map information becomes the next sentence’s topic. The laboratory rejected the first sample. A second sample was then requested. The voice changes, but the sequence remains coherent. The trial ended in May. The team now analyses the results. The trial ended in May. The team analysed the results. Both grammatical; the first describes current work, the second past work. A repeated opening can create clear thematic continuity; variation is a rhetorical choice, not a requirement to avoid the same subject three times. The bridge opened yesterday and carries traffic last year. The bridge opened yesterday and carries traffic now. The supplied times cannot describe an already functioning bridge last year if it first opened yesterday. The battery was empty. Therefore, the screen was brighter because of the empty battery. The battery was empty. The screen was brighter. Retain both stated observations while removing the unsupported causal assertion. The cause needs separate evidence; do not invent a different brightness event. topic continuity Keeping a participant or issue traceable across sentences. The lease expired. Its expiry ... given information Material assumed identifiable to the reader in context. the workshop in the second sentence source-2e5cd32b34733d source-eecf7dafccbf50 source-ca6ab50c9fe853 source-3cb07649187495

concepts.title: Academic compression, hedging and economical variety
concepts.definition: Grammatical compression expresses information with less explicit clausal structure; hedging adjusts commitment, scope or politeness. Neither compression nor formal vocabulary automatically improves a claim.

glossary.definition: Expressing an event, property or relation as a noun.
glossary.example: approve → approval

glossary.definition: An expression adjusting commitment, scope or directness.
glossary.example: The results may indicate ...

concepts.searchText: gv5-d26-m03 Academic compression, hedging and economical variety M N gv5-topic-d26-c07 gv5-topic-d26-c08 gv5-topic-d26-c09 Grammatical compression expresses information with less explicit clausal structure; hedging adjusts commitment, scope or politeness. Neither compression nor formal vocabulary automatically improves a claim. A verb can describe an event directly: The council approved the plan. A noun can package it for later discussion: This approval was unexpected. That change is nominalisation. It is useful when an earlier action becomes a new topic, or when a technical field needs an established concept. It can also conceal agents: approval of the plan leaves the approver unnamed. Ask which form gives readers the information they need. There is no universal rule that nouns are weak and verbs are strong. Compress only material whose contribution you understand. Because the samples were contaminated, the team repeated the test can become Because of sample contamination, the team repeated the test. The noun phrase is shorter, but it no longer states the contamination as a finite clause. A reduced relative can save words: the files that were damaged becomes the damaged files, though position and scope may change. Dense noun strings can obscure relations: student travel safety review may need a phrase explaining whose travel and what is being reviewed. A cautious academic claim can mark uncertainty (may explain), evidential limits (the interviews suggest), frequency (often) or scope (in the sampled schools). These are different contributions. Removing one can exaggerate the evidence. A narrow claim is not necessarily well-supported; it still needs evidence. Likewise, a figure supplies precision but is not automatically a hedge. Several qualifications can be necessary if they perform distinct jobs: The small sample suggests that the change may help some learners. Avoid stacking synonyms that add no further distinction. Syntactic variety serves clarity when each structure fits its information task. Active clauses can identify actors; passives can maintain a topic or appropriately background an unknown actor; nominalisations can organise an argument; explicit clauses can unpack compressed relations. Register belongs to a genre and audience rather than a hierarchy of longer words. A first-person statement of method can be appropriate in academic prose if the discipline permits it. An editor should distinguish grammatical defects, unsupported assertions and optional stylistic changes, then preserve modality, attribution and logical relationships while improving the text. clause → nominalisation + complement Packages an event for further discussion. evidence suggests that ... may ... Separates evidential support from modal possibility. The panel rejected the bid. This rejection delayed the project. The noun packages the earlier action as a topic. The interviews suggest that the policy may help new entrants. Suggest and may mark distinct aspects of commitment. Because the labels were missing, the samples could not be identified. An explicit causal clause can be clearer than a dense noun string. The treatment improves sleep. In this small trial, the treatment appeared to improve sleep. The second limits evidence and commitment; it is not interchangeable with the stronger claim. Purposeful repetition and a well-chosen passive may improve a text even when a shorter active alternative exists. The survey proves all workers prefer remote work; only twelve volunteers responded. The twelve volunteers’ responses suggest a preference for remote work within that small group. The original exceeds the supplied evidence in certainty and population scope. Due to the fact that the board made a decision to postpone the hearing, it was delayed. Because the board decided to postpone the hearing, it was delayed. The revision reduces avoidable wording while retaining the decision and consequence. nominalisation Expressing an event, property or relation as a noun. approve → approval hedge An expression adjusting commitment, scope or directness. The results may indicate ... source-a8b3fc5e4c8c96 source-3e3ac15bcaeafc source-f7c1a80292d10b

concepts.title: Summarising, précis and preserving essential qualifications
concepts.definition: A summary selects a text’s central message; a précis is a disciplined concise restatement under specified length and presentation constraints. Neither is a licence to invent facts or strengthen a claim.

glossary.definition: A concise restatement meeting a task’s specified constraints.
glossary.example: A 60-word account of a 180-word passage.

glossary.definition: A condition or limit affecting a claim.
glossary.example: mainly among secondary pupils

concepts.searchText: gv5-d27-m01 Summarising, précis and preserving essential qualifications N R gv5-topic-d27-c01 gv5-topic-d27-c05 gv5-topic-d27-c07 A summary selects a text’s central message; a précis is a disciplined concise restatement under specified length and presentation constraints. Neither is a licence to invent facts or strengthen a claim. Begin by identifying the source’s topic, main claim, supporting reasons and important limits. A summary is shorter because some detail is omitted, so the claim that every word or every fact must survive is unrealistic. What must survive is the source’s essential meaning at the requested level of detail. If the source says a measure may help some families, a summary saying the measure helps all families is inaccurate. A word target belongs to the assignment. One third is a common exercise convention, not a grammatical law for every summary. Separate a proposition from its examples. If a passage lists several dishes only to illustrate a varied menu, dishes may replace the list. If the passage argues that those particular foods caused an allergy, the exact list may matter. Classification words must not add evaluation: wheat and rice can become crops, but major crops asserts importance not supplied by the list alone. Preserve a condition when it limits the claim: free entry for registered students is not equivalent to free entry. Decide what to omit by its role in the argument, not by length alone. Use grammatical compression carefully. The applicants who were selected becomes the selected applicants when the selection meaning and intended scope remain clear. Because the tank leaked can become because of a tank leak. The rewrite may lose tense or explicit participants unless the surrounding text supplies them. A decision to act does not entail action: decided to close the school cannot become closed the school merely to save words. Likewise, not all changes are reversals: failed to confirm is weaker than denied. Compare the original and revision proposition by proposition. For an original reduction exercise, work from this fictional passage: A village library extended its Saturday opening for a six-week trial. Volunteers staffed the extra hour, so the council did not increase paid staffing. Visitor numbers rose during the trial, mainly among secondary-school pupils. However, the librarian warned that the period overlapped with examinations and was too short to show a lasting change. She recommended a longer trial before any permanent extension. A faithful brief summary reports the increased visits, volunteer arrangement and evidential caution. It must not claim the extension proved a permanent demand or that volunteers could necessarily sustain the arrangement indefinitely. source claim + essential restriction → shorter equivalent Retains who, what, scope and commitment while reducing wording. Selected applicants must attend an interview. The reduced relative identifies the selected group. The library’s trial coincided with examinations. This qualification limits interpretation of increased visits. Volunteer staffing accompanied a temporary extension, but a longer trial was recommended. The statement preserves the temporary arrangement and recommendation without claiming permanence. The committee decided to reopen the hall. The committee reopened the hall. Both grammatical; the second asserts action that the first alone does not entail. A short summary can omit illustrative detail while retaining essential meaning; a task demanding exact equivalence permits fewer omissions. The trial proves that all pupils need longer hours. The short trial recorded more visits, mainly by secondary pupils; its timing limits conclusions. The original passage supports neither proof nor a universal need. The trial was short, it overlapped with examinations. The trial was short and overlapped with examinations. Joining two independent clauses with only a comma creates a splice in ordinary formal prose. précis A concise restatement meeting a task’s specified constraints. A 60-word account of a 180-word passage. qualification A condition or limit affecting a claim. mainly among secondary pupils source-a8b3fc5e4c8c96 source-43b3913aec1e91 source-3e3ac15bcaeafc

concepts.title: Paraphrase, synthesis and faithful reported claims
concepts.definition: Paraphrase re-expresses a source’s message; synthesis relates messages from more than one source. Both require grammatical accuracy and faithful treatment of time, modality, attribution and logical relations.

glossary.definition: A reasoned combination of claims from different sources.
glossary.example: One study found ...; another found ...

glossary.definition: A meaning that must hold if a statement is true in its intended reading.
glossary.example: They left entails that a departure occurred under the ordinary event reading.

concepts.searchText: gv5-d27-m02 Paraphrase, synthesis and faithful reported claims N R gv5-topic-d27-c02 gv5-topic-d27-c04 gv5-topic-d27-c06 Paraphrase re-expresses a source’s message; synthesis relates messages from more than one source. Both require grammatical accuracy and faithful treatment of time, modality, attribution and logical relations. A paraphrase can alter sentence structure, word choice and information order while preserving the relevant proposition. The team postponed the launch because the battery failed can become Battery failure caused the team to postpone the launch. Both identify the same actor, event and cause. Replacing words with dictionary synonyms without checking their grammatical patterns can produce errors. Depend on does not become depend from because another language uses a different relation word. Keep the source available while checking meaning, then use independent wording rather than copying its sentence and replacing a few words. Track tense and aspect. The plant has closed presents closure with current relevance; the plant closed in March locates a completed event at a specified past time. Either can fit a paraphrase when the necessary time information is retained, but adding March without a source invents a fact. Track modality too: must may express an obligation or a deduction, while may can express permission or possibility. The school may close is not the same as the school must close. Scope matters: not every application succeeded means some failed, not that none succeeded. A synthesis must distinguish agreement, difference and silence. Source A says the scheme reduced travel time in two towns; Source B says ticket costs rose. A combined sentence can report both, but cannot claim costs rose because travel time fell unless a source establishes that relationship. Attribution can be compressed without vanishing: According to the survey ... or The authors argue ... identifies whose claim is reported. A reporting verb such as prove, admit or concede may add evidential or evaluative meaning absent from the source. Retain neutral said, report or find when stronger force is unjustified. Meaning preservation includes entailments and implications. A transformation that makes a restrictive relative supplementary may imply that every member of a group has the property. Removing only or changing the position of a negative can alter scope while leaving the sentence fluent. A paraphrase does not need to reproduce all rhetorical emphasis, but a task may require preserving contrast, caution or a writer’s stance. In expert revision, list the propositions before comparing sentences: actor, action, affected participant, time, quantifier, modality, source and connection. Where two readings remain possible, explain the ambiguity rather than certify a single equivalent mechanically. Source A reports X, whereas Source B reports Y Makes differing attributed claims explicit. not every + noun Denies universality rather than asserting universal failure. The report suggests that costs may fall. Attribution and possibility both remain visible. Not every licence was renewed. At least one was not renewed; the sentence does not say none were. The first survey found shorter journeys; the second recorded higher fares. The synthesis relates results without inventing a causal link. No applications succeeded. Not all applications succeeded. The first excludes every success; the second permits some successes. A past source can be reported in a present reporting frame when its argument is treated as current; preserve the events’ actual time relations. The report suggests a benefit. → The report proves a benefit. The report indicates a possible benefit. Proves strengthens evidential commitment without support. Only registered readers borrowed the maps. → Registered readers borrowed only the maps. Only registered readers borrowed the maps. Moving only changes its focus from the readers to the objects borrowed. synthesis A reasoned combination of claims from different sources. One study found ...; another found ... entailment A meaning that must hold if a statement is true in its intended reading. They left entails that a departure occurred under the ordinary event reading. source-3e3ac15bcaeafc source-43b3913aec1e91 source-89176b529bbc02

concepts.title: Translation and formal written answers
concepts.definition: Grammatical translation conveys the intended message through the target language’s own constructions. Formal expression selects structures appropriate to a purpose and audience while retaining meaning.

glossary.definition: Language choices associated with a situation, purpose and audience.
glossary.example: a formal request

glossary.definition: The language into which a message is translated.
glossary.example: English in this exercise

concepts.searchText: gv5-d27-m03 Translation and formal written answers N R gv5-topic-d27-c03 gv5-topic-d27-c08 Grammatical translation conveys the intended message through the target language’s own constructions. Formal expression selects structures appropriate to a purpose and audience while retaining meaning. Translation is not a word-by-word substitution exercise. Languages differ in word order, agreement, articles, pronouns, tense-aspect patterns and conventional combinations. Begin with a plain account of the intended meaning, including who acts and when. Then construct an English sentence from that meaning. A language without English-style articles does not supply an automatic equivalent for a and the; decide whether the English referent is countable and identifiable. Learners can use any first language for this analysis. Urdu-based examples are useful options, not assumptions about every learner’s background. For a controlled translation exercise, the source message can be specified in plain meaning notes instead of requiring knowledge of another language. Message: speaker lives in Multan; residence began in 2019 and continues. Suitable English includes I have lived in Multan since 2019 and I have been living in Multan since 2019. The progressive highlights duration or ongoing activity; the simple perfect is also standard. A literal I am living ... since 2019 is not the ordinary edited pattern for that intended continuing interval. Check meaning and idiom rather than matching one model string. Formal correspondence needs clear participants, actions, dates and requested responses. Please send the revised form by Friday is often clearer than a chain of nominalisations. A form such as We request that the form be returned by Friday is also grammatical and may suit a formal institution. The audience determines register; first person, contractions and ordinary short verbs are not universal grammar errors. Regional expressions can be established within their communities while unfamiliar elsewhere. For international readers, choose transparent wording and explain why, instead of treating the regional speaker as grammatically incapable. Academic answers must distinguish a source’s assertion from the writer’s interpretation. In The author argues that restrictions may reduce demand, the writer reports a cautious claim; changing may to will increases commitment. In translation and paraphrase, preserve negation, quantity, politeness, evidential status and temporal relations even if the new sentence uses a different voice. Back-translation can expose a mismatch, but it is not proof of exact equivalence because several expressions may encode a message. A good rubric recognises alternatives and evaluates specified features. It must not pretend that comparison with a model objectively grades an independently written passage. meaning notes → idiomatic target construction Uses English grammar to express the intended message. request + action + deadline Makes formal correspondence actionable. Please return the signed declaration by Thursday. The action, document and deadline are explicit. I have lived in Multan since 2019. The present perfect expresses continuing residence from a past starting point. The authors argue that the policy may reduce waste. The report preserves source and possibility rather than presenting a proven result. Kindly intimate the office. Please inform the office. The second is more transparent for a broad audience; register and regional convention must be distinguished from grammaticality. A regional expression can be standard in its variety; choosing a wider-audience alternative is an editorial decision, not proof of universal error. We request you that send the form. We request that you send the form. The source mixes two complement patterns. The letter says all applicant must signs. The letter says all applicants must sign. All takes plural applicants here; a modal takes the base verb sign. register Language choices associated with a situation, purpose and audience. a formal request target language The language into which a message is translated. English in this exercise source-f7c1a80292d10b source-ca6ab50c9fe853 source-10e4340e83d799

concepts.title: Diagnose the relationship before changing the words
concepts.definition: Grammatical error analysis identifies a problematic relationship, explains the applicable construction and checks whether a proposed repair is supported by the intended meaning. An unusual form is not itself proof of an error.

glossary.definition: An evidence-based explanation of a problematic grammatical relationship.
glossary.example: quality ... have → quality ... has

glossary.definition: An unnecessary change that treats a defensible construction as faulty.
glossary.example: rejecting all plural committee agreement

concepts.searchText: gv5-d28-m01 Diagnose the relationship before changing the words Q R gv5-topic-d28-c01 gv5-topic-d28-c02 gv5-topic-d28-c09 Grammatical error analysis identifies a problematic relationship, explains the applicable construction and checks whether a proposed repair is supported by the intended meaning. An unusual form is not itself proof of an error. Read the complete context before selecting a correction. Identify the main clauses, their subjects and finite verb phrases, then examine the relationships inside them. In The quality of the reports have improved, quality is the singular head of the subject and has is the conventional agreement repair. In The reports have improved in quality, the plural verb is already correct. The same vocabulary therefore supports different grammatical analyses. State the relationship that fails rather than pointing to the nearest unfamiliar word. Separate a confirmed error from missing information. In Amina told Salma that her proposal was accepted, her can refer to either woman unless context settles the reference. The sentence is not structurally ungrammatical, but a report may need explicit naming. In The committee have submitted their views, British member-oriented agreement is possible, so a correction to has/its must be justified by intended unit reference or a specified editorial system. A diagnostic note should say whether the issue is agreement, reference, scope, complementation, punctuation, meaning or register. Some sentences contain more than one fault. The findings was presented very clear contains plural-subject agreement and an adjective–adverb problem for the intended description of presentation. Repairing only was leaves the second issue. Conversely, changing every marked expression can introduce errors or change tone unnecessarily. Use a staged record: original wording, intended meaning, diagnosed relation, minimum adequate repair, alternative repair and limiting exception. Minimum means sufficient to solve the stated problem, not always the fewest written characters or an obligation to retain a misleading structure. Evidence-sensitive analysis remains open to alternative frameworks. Traditional accounts may call an -ing construction a gerund phrase where a modern account analyses a non-finite clause. If both identify the same form, internal subject relationship and external function, terminology alone need not invalidate an answer. When authorities differ, ask whether they describe different registers, national conventions, senses or theoretical categories. Do not invent a source citation to make a judgement look final. Where context supports more than one correction, list the alternatives and state which meaning each preserves. context → structure → disputed relationship → repair → verification Makes the reasoning behind an edit explicit. one sentence → possibly several independent diagnoses A task may contain multiple genuine faults; identify each rather than stopping automatically after one. The list of entries is incomplete. Singular list controls is despite plural entries inside the of-phrase. The officer found the account convincing. Convincing functions as an object complement describing the account. The committee have discussed their individual objections. Member-oriented British agreement is defensible; unfamiliar plural agreement is not enough to prove error. The findings were presented very clearly. The findings were very clear. Both are grammatical but different: the first describes presentation manner; the second describes the findings themselves. A grammatical sentence can still be ambiguous, misleading or unsuitable for an audience. Diagnose that actual problem instead of inventing a syntactic fault. The number of visitors have increased. The number of visitors has increased. Number heads a singular measure expression here. She explained me the procedure. She explained the procedure to me. Explain takes the topic as direct object and ordinarily marks this recipient with to. error diagnosis An evidence-based explanation of a problematic grammatical relationship. quality ... have → quality ... has overcorrection An unnecessary change that treats a defensible construction as faulty. rejecting all plural committee agreement source-287989cd31ff3a source-58353073c867f7 source-5e8743788d0639 source-f7c1a80292d10b

concepts.title: Reconstruction with a meaning ledger
concepts.definition: A meaning ledger records the information a transformation must preserve: participants, event, time, polarity, quantity, modality and logical relationship. Reconstruction changes form while checking these features explicitly.

glossary.definition: The part of an expression affected by negation, focus or another operator.
glossary.example: only the clerk versus only the forms

glossary.definition: A conclusion that follows from a statement’s meaning if that statement is true.
glossary.example: She left entails that her leaving occurred.

concepts.searchText: gv5-d28-m02 Reconstruction with a meaning ledger Q R gv5-topic-d28-c03 gv5-topic-d28-c04 gv5-topic-d28-c05 A meaning ledger records the information a transformation must preserve: participants, event, time, polarity, quantity, modality and logical relationship. Reconstruction changes form while checking these features explicitly. Start with who did what, when and with what degree of commitment. Hana may submit the report tomorrow does not mean Hana will submit it, and Hana did not submit it does not mean that nobody did. When combining sentences, choose a connector justified by the source: The lights failed. The session ended early permits a simple and combination without proving that one caused the other. A because combination needs a supplied causal relationship. Sentence splitting must preserve a concession, condition or limitation rather than leaving two loosely associated claims. Transformations offer several structural resources: active and passive voice, finite and non-finite clauses, relative clauses, nominalisation, coordination and marked order. Each has restrictions. A passive normally needs a compatible verb construction, and it must retain an identified agent when that identity matters. The assessor rejected the appeal can become The appeal was rejected by the assessor. A shortened The appeal was rejected omits the named actor, so it may be unsuitable in an exact-content transformation. Fronting or clefting may preserve the central proposition while adding focus or a presuppositional effect. Word-order reconstruction requires hierarchy, not just arranging familiar neighbours. Identify which words form a noun phrase, which auxiliaries precede the lexical verb and which clause a modifier belongs to. Only the clerk checked the forms and The clerk checked only the forms place the focus restriction on different constituents. Keep a negative with the intended scope. Not all candidates passed allows some passes; no candidates passed excludes every pass. If a transformation silently exchanges these, grammatical fluency cannot repair the changed meaning. After writing a candidate reconstruction, compare its entailments with the source. Decided to leave does not entail left; advised her to leave does not entail that she obeyed; failed to leave does entail that the intended leaving did not occur. Avoid replacing an uncertain source with an authoritative-sounding nominalisation such as the proven failure. Some tasks demand only preservation of a central proposition, while others require close semantic equivalence. State which standard applies, especially when an inversion, cleft, nominalisation or passive changes emphasis, reference accessibility or assumed background. source proposition + ledger → reconstructed structure + ledger check Tests meaning as well as formal correctness. not all X → partial negation; no X → total exclusion The two quantificational claims are not equivalent. The appeal was rejected by the assessor. The passive preserves the named participants of The assessor rejected the appeal. Although costs rose, access improved. Combining the two claims with although presents an explicitly supplied concession. What the team needed was a longer trial. A pseudo-cleft foregrounds the requested remedy; it is not always pragmatically identical to neutral order. The witness decided to withdraw her statement. The witness withdrew her statement. Both are grammatical, but the first reports a decision and the second a completed action; they are not equivalent. A grammatically successful transformation can legitimately change focus when the task asks for emphasis. A close-equivalence task must acknowledge that added effect rather than claim that nothing changes. Original says some failed; rewrite says None passed. Not all passed. At least one did not pass; this does not establish how many passed and remains compatible with nobody passing. Original names the inspector; rewrite omits the agent from The file was examined. The file was examined by the inspector. Retain the named actor when the task requires all source information. scope The part of an expression affected by negation, focus or another operator. only the clerk versus only the forms entailment A conclusion that follows from a statement’s meaning if that statement is true. She left entails that her leaving occurred. source-3cb07649187495 source-43b3913aec1e91 source-897ffbdb4059a3 source-028b7ffa729def source-10e4340e83d799

concepts.title: Suspicious but grammatical: context and register
concepts.definition: A suspicious construction is one a learner expects to be wrong because it is unfamiliar, formal, informal or variable. A defensible judgement examines its licensing context and intended reading before applying a preferred rewrite.

glossary.definition: A construction differing from the neutral order for a recognised effect.
glossary.example: Never had she seen it.

glossary.definition: The defensibility of a form under its intended interpretation and situation.
glossary.example: being difficult as temporary behaviour

concepts.searchText: gv5-d28-m03 Suspicious but grammatical: context and register Q R gv5-topic-d28-c06 gv5-topic-d28-c07 A suspicious construction is one a learner expects to be wrong because it is unfamiliar, formal, informal or variable. A defensible judgement examines its licensing context and intended reading before applying a preferred rewrite. A sentence can already be correct even when a memorised classroom rule predicts trouble. This is the person I spoke to uses standard preposition stranding. It was me uses an ordinary standard object-form complement after be, while it was I belongs to a more formal style. Neither familiarity nor personal preference decides every grammatical question. When a task offers no change, consider it seriously. Identify a rule actually broken in the stated context; do not assume the exercise setter must have hidden a fault. Marked word order can be fully grammatical. Rarely have we seen such detail uses inversion after a fronted negative-frequency adjunct. Only Aisha knew the code has no inversion because only modifies the subject, whereas Only after the briefing did Aisha know the code fronts a restrictive adjunct. Reported questions use their own structure: By whom the document was signed remains unknown contains an embedded interrogative functioning as subject; it is not a direct question requiring Was the document signed ...? The whole clause’s function determines the pattern. Regional, register and contextual alternatives need explicit labels. The committee are divided is acceptable British member agreement. I have just finished and the American I just finished can both be standard in suitable contexts. Mandative should in They insisted that he should attend is standard British usage. Informal or ordinary object who does not become automatically wrong because the more formal whom exists. An editor can still choose a more formal variant for a specified purpose, but that decision should be described as an editorial preference rather than a correction of universal grammar. Some apparent anomalies depend on a different lexical sense. She is being difficult gives a temporary behavioural reading, so a blanket prohibition on progressive be or all stative expressions fails. The researcher effected a change uses a legitimate verb meaning brought about. Historical prescriptive slogans can be useful reminders in limited contexts, but a reliable analysis identifies those limits. In a formal examination practice item, avoid giving two standard variants and asking for the only correct one unless the convention or meaning is supplied. In open analysis, explain why no repair is necessary and offer an optional recast separately. marked construction + licensing context An unusual order may be required or licensed by a recognised construction. standard variant + stated register/region A different preferred form does not automatically make the source incorrect. Rarely did the visitors complain. Negative-adjunct fronting licenses auxiliary inversion. By whom the permit was issued remains uncertain.
