The embedded interrogative is the subject of remains; its internal order is defensible. The committee are considering their separate objections. Plural member reference is licensed in British English. Only Nida had the key. Only after noon did Nida have the key. Both are grammatical; only has different attachment and the fronted adjunct licenses inversion in the second. A stated specialist or house-style rule can require one standard variant for that assignment. Explain its scope rather than extending it to all English. Rarely we had encountered such delays. Rarely had we encountered such delays. Here rarely is a fronted negative-frequency adjunct and the formal pattern uses inversion. She asked where did I work. She asked where I worked. Ordinary formal embedded-question order differs from direct-question inversion. marked structure A construction differing from the neutral order for a recognised effect. Never had she seen it. grammatical acceptability in context The defensibility of a form under its intended interpretation and situation. being difficult as temporary behaviour source-f36cfc25889ed4 source-8cf60a1688508e source-89176b529bbc02 source-5e8743788d0639 source-f3988fbed0a134 source-f7c1a80292d10b

concepts.title: Paragraph editing and explicit editorial reasoning
concepts.definition: Paragraph editing examines local sentence grammar together with reference, temporal relations and logical connections across the text. A successful edit preserves the author’s supportable message while making the expression accurate and clear.

glossary.definition: A reason connecting an edit to grammar, meaning or stated style.
glossary.example: Changing was to were for plural users.

glossary.definition: A revision retaining the relevant source propositions and qualifications.
glossary.example: some advice was posted

concepts.searchText: gv5-d28-m04 Paragraph editing and explicit editorial reasoning Q R gv5-topic-d28-c08 Paragraph editing examines local sentence grammar together with reference, temporal relations and logical connections across the text. A successful edit preserves the author’s supportable message while making the expression accurate and clear. Read a paragraph once for its intended message before repairing details. Identify the participants and events, then check whether pronouns, tense choices and connectors allow a reader to track them. The goal is not to make every verb share one tense. A current report can explain an earlier trial and a future recommendation. Nor must every paragraph use one voice. An active sentence may introduce an actor while a passive sentence continues discussion of the affected object. Explain a change in terms of the text’s information, not a general ban. Use a worked original paragraph. Draft: The library tested a new booking system last month. Its users was asked to reserve seats online, and several advice were posted near the desk. The report suggests that the system may reduce waiting, although only twelve visitors answered the survey. The team will collect more evidence before it makes a permanent decision. A restrained edit changes users was to users were and several advice were to several pieces of advice were. It keeps may, although and only twelve because those words limit the claim. Classify each change. Users/were is agreement; pieces of advice repairs ordinary countability and preserves plurality through pieces; may is modal uncertainty; only twelve identifies a small response group without proving that no other visitors existed. Do not change suggests/may into proves/will merely to sound confident. The last sentence’s future form is compatible with the past trial and present report. Before it makes uses a present form in an ordinary future time clause. These relationships show why a grammatical paragraph can contain several time references. An editorial report should quote the problematic wording, explain the principle, give a corrected form and identify alternatives when meaningful. concepts.title: Read the evidence report and choose a precise revision action

concepts.title: Negation, polarity and quantifier scope
concepts.definition: Negation rejects a proposition or a relevant part of its meaning. Scope is the portion of a structure or interpretation affected by an operator such as not, every or only. Surface word order is evidence for scope, but context and prosody can also matter.

glossary.definition: The part of an interpretation affected by an operator.
glossary.example: Not all rejected differs from all rejected.

glossary.definition: Multiple negative forms associated with a single semantic negation in a variety.
glossary.example: Some dialects use I didn’t see nobody for I saw nobody.

glossary.definition: An expression whose distribution or interpretation is sensitive to environments such as negation or questions.
glossary.example: Any in I did not see any is licensed in a negative context.

concepts.searchText: gv5-ref-negation-scope Negation, polarity and quantifier scope D K P gv5-ref-k01 gv5-ref-k02 gv5-ref-k03 Negation rejects a proposition or a relevant part of its meaning. Scope is the portion of a structure or interpretation affected by an operator such as not, every or only. Surface word order is evidence for scope, but context and prosody can also matter. English commonly forms a negative finite clause with not after an auxiliary: The clerk has not replied. Where an ordinary lexical verb has no auxiliary, do-support is normally used: The clerk did not reply. Be can itself carry negation: The office is not open. A negative subject can make the clause negative without an additional negative verb: Nobody replied. Do not add didn’t simply because the intended message is negative. The difference between no and not is structural as well as semantic: no can determine a noun phrase, as in no reply, whereas not commonly negates a clause or phrase. These examples describe ordinary standard constructions, not every historically or regionally established pattern. Scope changes meaning. Not all applications were successful means that at least one was unsuccessful; it does not by itself assert that any succeeded. No applications were successful states zero success. In an everyday conversation, a speaker saying not all may encourage an inference that some did succeed, but that extra inference should not be built into an exact answer key without context. All the applications were not successful can be unclear between intended readings for some audiences; revise explicitly when the distinction matters. Quantified noun phrases can also interact: Every reviewer read a report can allow a different report for each reviewer or one report shared by all. A careful paraphrase states the intended relationship. Any, ever and related expressions occur naturally in many negative, interrogative and conditional environments: I did not find any errors; Did you find any?; If you find any, call me. They are not exclusively negative words. Free-choice any in Any qualified applicant may apply has a different distribution and interpretation. Negative concord, as in dialectal I didn’t see nobody with one intended negation, is a systematic feature of some varieties; it is not ordinarily the edited standard British or American pattern taught as the course default. For that default, use I didn’t see anybody or I saw nobody. Distinguish this concord from two independently meaningful negatives, such as It is not impossible. Logical paraphrase is useful but not a replacement for actual usage. Not impossible leaves possibility open; it does not guarantee likelihood or success. Negative questions often convey expectations, and an answer should clarify the proposition: Yes, she called or No, she did not call. Focus and contrast can narrow negation: I did not criticise the design because it was expensive may deny the criticism or deny that expense was the reason, depending on context. An assessment must stipulate the intended reading or ask learners to explain the ambiguity. Formal writing benefits from explicit scope when costs, obligations or permissions depend on it; unfamiliarity alone does not make a negative construction ungrammatical. not all + plural noun phrase Denies universal inclusion; it does not entail a positive number within the group. no + noun phrase / auxiliary + not + remaining verb phrase Negative noun-phrase determination and clause negation have different structures. Not all the windows were locked. At least one window was not locked; the sentence alone does not say how many were locked. No windows were locked. This states zero locked windows in the relevant set. Each inspector received a different folder. Different makes an intended distribution explicit, rather than leaving it to the scope of an indefinite folder. The plan is not impossible. The plan will probably succeed. The first rejects impossibility. It does not entail the probability judgement in the second. Any also has free-choice uses outside negative environments, so never define it as a word used only in negatives or questions. Multiple negative forms may express dialectal negative concord, litotes or genuinely separate negations. Identify the construction and editorial target before revising. Not all passed means that some definitely passed. Not all passed entails that universal passing did not occur; it can be true if nobody passed. A common conversational suggestion is not the same as an entailment. I didn’t see nobody is meaningless in every variety. For edited standard English, use I didn’t see anybody; some dialects systematically use negative concord. Register/variety is the issue, not absence of linguistic structure. scope The part of an interpretation affected by an operator. Not all rejected differs from all rejected. negative concord Multiple negative forms associated with a single semantic negation in a variety. Some dialects use I didn’t see nobody for I saw nobody. polarity item An expression whose distribution or interpretation is sensitive to environments such as negation or questions. Any in I did not see any is licensed in a negative context. source-c5aeee4ead1514 source-a3c15737ad3e61 source-c6656ba16f39b1

concepts.title: Presupposition, entailment and contextual interpretation
concepts.definition: A presupposition is information an utterance normally treats as already taken for granted, often associated with a particular expression. An entailment follows from what is asserted under the relevant reading. Pragmatic inferences also depend on context, expectations and the purpose of the utterance.

glossary.definition: Information an utterance normally treats as taken for granted under a reading.
glossary.example: Stopped visiting commonly backgrounds earlier visits.

glossary.definition: A consequence that must hold if the asserted proposition is true under the relevant reading.
glossary.example: All members voted entails that each member in the relevant group voted.

glossary.definition: Adjusting contextual assumptions to interpret information presented as already shared.
glossary.example: A reader may infer a previously unmentioned gate from the side gate.

concepts.searchText: gv5-ref-presupposition Presupposition, entailment and contextual interpretation K M N gv5-ref-k04 gv5-ref-k05 gv5-ref-k06 A presupposition is information an utterance normally treats as already taken for granted, often associated with a particular expression. An entailment follows from what is asserted under the relevant reading. Pragmatic inferences also depend on context, expectations and the purpose of the utterance. Compare Leena opened the gate with Leena has stopped opening the gate at dawn. The first asserts an opening event. The second normally takes a previous practice for granted while asserting its cessation. A reader who never knew of that practice may accommodate it: provisionally add it to the shared information. Accommodation is an interpretation process, not independent evidence that the practice existed. In factual academic or professional writing, do not smuggle an unverified premise into a sentence merely by presenting it as familiar. Ask what the source explicitly states, what it presupposes and what the writer is only inferring. The grammatical form can influence these distinctions without guaranteeing real-world truth. Expressions often discussed as presupposition triggers include stop, again, definite descriptions and factive predicates such as regret. The coordinator regrets that the hearing was postponed normally treats the postponement as a fact while reporting an attitude toward it. Negating the attitude usually leaves that background assumption: The coordinator does not regret that the hearing was postponed. This persistence under negation is a useful diagnostic, not an exceptionless definition. Questions and conditionals provide further tests, and interpretations can depend on local context. Again commonly signals recurrence, but its exact attachment and focus can matter. Do not turn a short list of triggers into a mechanical method that ignores the whole sentence. Entailment and conversational inference require different reasoning. Some applicants arrived late is compatible with all applicants arriving late under its basic existential reading, although ordinary conversation often suggests not all. By contrast, The applicants all arrived late entails arrival for each member of the relevant group under that reading. A stronger statement cannot automatically be substituted for a weaker source statement in a précis. Likewise, The service was not unhelpful can convey restrained praise without being equivalent in tone or commitment to The service was excellent. Grammar provides possible structures; register and conversational expectations help explain why a writer chooses one rather than another. Preserve both propositional qualifications and the force of cautious claims when paraphrasing. Presupposition research contains substantive theoretical disagreements about conventional meaning, speaker assumptions, projection and cancellation. This course introduces practical diagnostics rather than claiming one short account resolves those debates. Presuppositions sometimes fail to project through a larger structure, and a continuation can reject or suspend an apparent background assumption. It is therefore safer to say normally presupposes under this reading than always proves. In editing, a loaded question such as Who approved the alteration? may invite the assumption that somebody did, while Nobody approved it rejects that assumption. The response is not grammatically defective merely because it declines the proposed premise. Expert analysis specifies the reading, context and evidence, and distinguishes grammatical acceptability from the truth or fairness of the assumption. X regrets that P Normally presents P as a background fact while asserting X’s regret. X has stopped doing Y Normally backgrounds earlier Y-activity while asserting that the activity has ceased. The caretaker has stopped opening the side gate. Earlier opening is normally backgrounded; cessation is asserted. The caretaker has not stopped opening the side gate. The negative commonly preserves the assumption of earlier opening while rejecting cessation. If there ever was a side gate, the caretaker no longer uses it. The explicit conditional context can suspend existence assumptions that a simpler definite description might encourage. Some reviewers requested revisions. All reviewers requested revisions. The first does not entail the second. An expectation that some excludes all is not a universal truth-conditional rule. Projection and cancellation vary by trigger, embedding and context; a single negation test is not a complete proof. Backgrounding a claim does not verify it. Source-based writing must check the factual premise as well as the grammar. The source says visits rose during the trial; therefore the trial caused the increase. Visits rose during the trial; the source does not by itself establish the cause. A temporal relation does not entail a causal relation. Closed always entails that it had previously been open. A stative description such as The office is closed need not entail prior openness; an eventive reading needs its own context. Do not add the presupposition no longer without evidence for a change of state. presupposition Information an utterance normally treats as taken for granted under a reading. Stopped visiting commonly backgrounds earlier visits. entailment A consequence that must hold if the asserted proposition is true under the relevant reading. All members voted entails that each member in the relevant group voted. accommodation Adjusting contextual assumptions to interpret information presented as already shared. A reader may infer a previously unmentioned gate from the side gate. source-a83d66871c2ac7 source-a3c15737ad3e61

concepts.title: Word formation beyond prefixes and suffixes
concepts.definition: Word formation creates or establishes lexemes: vocabulary items with related grammatical forms. Affixation, compounding, conversion, clipping, blending and back-formation describe different processes; a word can participate in more than one process across its history.

glossary.definition: A vocabulary item considered together with its grammatical forms.
glossary.example: Write, writes, wrote and written can be forms of the lexeme write.

glossary.definition: Establishing a different word class without an overt derivational affix.
glossary.example: A host / to host a meeting.

glossary.definition: A historically new expression formed by reanalysing and removing apparent word-building material.
glossary.example: Edit was formed from editor.

concepts.searchText: gv5-ref-morph-processes Word formation beyond prefixes and suffixes A L gv5-ref-a01 gv5-ref-a02 gv5-ref-a03 gv5-ref-a04 gv5-ref-a05 Word formation creates or establishes lexemes: vocabulary items with related grammatical forms. Affixation, compounding, conversion, clipping, blending and back-formation describe different processes; a word can participate in more than one process across its history. Begin by separating a change in grammatical form from the creation of a vocabulary item. In The editors work and The editor works, works belongs to the verb work and marks a grammatical contrast. In They edit and The editor arrived, editor is a separate noun related to edit. Inflection supplies forms within a lexeme; derivation contributes a related lexeme. These useful distinctions do not mean every suffix changes word class: an abstract noun can be derived from another noun. Nor does every newly established word contain a visible prefix or suffix. Always examine its category and meaning in a complete expression, then ask which operation the analysis is intended to describe. Affixation adds a bound element to a base, as in readable or unreadable. Compounding combines lexical bases, as in school library or proofreader; spaces and hyphens do not by themselves decide whether an expression is a compound. Conversion establishes a different category without an overt derivational affix: a bottle contrasts with They bottle the juice. Clipping shortens an existing word: photo is a shortened form of photograph, and exam of examination. A blend combines material from source words, as in brunch from breakfast and lunch. A blend differs from an ordinary compound because its source words need not remain intact; some borderline formations resist one simple label. Back-formation produces a new expression by analysing an existing word as if it contained removable material. The historical relationship matters: edit developed from editor, rather than editor historically being made by adding a suffix to an already established English edit. In present-day grammatical analysis, however, speakers can understand editor as edit plus an agent-forming ending. Historical origin and a contemporary structural relationship are therefore different questions. Do not infer a word’s actual history merely because one expression is shorter. Initialisms such as BBC and word-pronounced acronyms such as NATO also establish shortened expressions, but use initial letters rather than simply removing syllables from one word. Pronunciation helps distinguish these categories. Word-formation labels describe patterns, not automatic permission to publish any possible coinage as established vocabulary. A creative conversion or blend may be interpretable in advertising yet unsuitable without explanation in an academic report. Lexicalisation means an expression becomes established with particular meanings or restrictions; those meanings need not be completely predictable from its parts. Compound stress and semantic relations are useful evidence, but neither produces an infallible test across all English compounds. In specialist discussion, conversion is sometimes analysed using a zero derivational element, while other analyses treat category change without such an element. This theoretical difference does not require learners to invent an inaudible suffix in an ordinary sentence analysis. base + affix → related lexeme The relation is derivational when it establishes a lexical item rather than simply a grammatical form. noun used as lexical verb: bottle → bottle Conversion changes category in the stated use without an overt affix. The technician photographed the damaged panel. Photographed is a past form of the verb photograph; the ending supplies inflection. The technician emailed a photo of the panel. Photo is a clipping, while emailed uses the verb email with past inflection. More than one process can be relevant to a sentence. The journal’s editor asked us to edit the abstract. Historically edit is a back-formation from editor; synchronically the two belong to a recognisable noun–verb family. a school library a brunch menu School library is a lexical-base combination; brunch itself is a blend. The whole expression brunch menu can in turn function as a noun compound. Not every abbreviation is spoken in its shortened written form. Dr is normally read as doctor; exam is ordinarily spoken as exam. Word-class conversion and syntactic function must remain distinct: stone in stone wall can be a noun modifier without becoming an adjective. Every shorter word is a back-formation. A shorter word may be a clipping, an unrelated word or a documented back-formation. Historical evidence is needed for the direction of a back-formation. School library cannot be a compound because it has a space. A compound may be written open, hyphenated or closed. Orthography varies and is not a sufficient structural diagnostic. lexeme A vocabulary item considered together with its grammatical forms. Write, writes, wrote and written can be forms of the lexeme write. conversion Establishing a different word class without an overt derivational affix. A host / to host a meeting. back-formation A historically new expression formed by reanalysing and removing apparent word-building material. Edit was formed from editor. source-c81befbecce753 source-50a90a203e61ad source-b2b7332c9f54f4 source-14981994c4d0b7 source-abb4eb7aa69725

concepts.title: Roots, affix order and grammatical productivity
concepts.definition: Productivity is the extent to which a grammatical or word-building pattern can be extended to additional suitable forms. It is constrained by category, meaning, sound, history and established vocabulary; it is not the claim that every imaginable combination is equally acceptable.

glossary.definition: A variant realisation of one morpheme.
glossary.example: The regular plural has different sounds in cats and dogs.

glossary.definition: The capacity of a pattern to extend to additional suitable forms.
glossary.example: A speaker can use a familiar noun in a newly motivated verb use.

glossary.definition: A form to which a morphological operation applies.
glossary.example: Unhelpful is the base for -ness in unhelpfulness.

concepts.searchText: gv5-ref-morph-productivity Roots, affix order and grammatical productivity A K gv5-ref-a06 gv5-ref-a07 gv5-ref-a08 Productivity is the extent to which a grammatical or word-building pattern can be extended to additional suitable forms. It is constrained by category, meaning, sound, history and established vocabulary; it is not the claim that every imaginable combination is equally acceptable. A root is the central lexical element in an analysis. A base is any form to which an operation applies, while a stem is a form used as the base for inflection. In teachers, teach is a root, teacher is the stem receiving plural -s, and teacher is also a base for that operation. Terminology can vary between descriptions, so state which operation you mean. A bound morpheme cannot normally stand alone in its relevant use; a free morpheme can. Visible spelling pieces do not automatically correspond to meaningful morphemes: the letters er in a word are not necessarily the agent suffix found in teacher. Repeated form and a consistent grammatical relationship provide stronger evidence than appearance alone. Affix order can show hierarchical structure. In unhelpfulness, -ful first relates to help, un- negates helpful, and -ness produces the abstract noun. This analysis concerns relationships, not just a list of neighbouring letters. The plural of a derived count noun usually applies outside the derivation: teacher → teachers. Inflection may also involve an irregular change rather than a simple added segment: mouse → mice. An allomorph is an alternative form of a morpheme; English plural endings have different pronunciations in cats, dogs and buses. The spelling may look similar while the sound differs, and one grammatical category can have more than one formal realisation. A productive pattern remains open to suitable new formations, but productivity is gradual. The suffix -ness combines readily with many adjectives, whereas some other suffixes are restricted to established lexical families. Comprehensibility does not guarantee conventional status: a reader may understand a novel coinage while a learner’s dictionary recommends an established alternative for ordinary formal writing. Existing words can compete with potential regular formations; ordinary standard past went is not replaced by goed merely because regular verbs take -ed. Such cases show why a structural pattern is a starting point for analysis rather than a complete lexical authority. Check the intended meaning and established usage before declaring a new-looking form correct or incorrect. Morphological and syntactic structure can interact without being identical. A compound may have an internal head that determines its category or main semantic type, but exceptional or historically opaque compounds need separate lexical attention. A present-day speaker’s analysis may differ from an etymologist’s account, and plausible segmentation is not proof of historical origin. Word-building also changes over time: material in a blend or a borrowed item can become available for further coinages. An advanced analysis should therefore distinguish productivity, frequency, transparency and lexicalisation. A frequent word need not exemplify a productive rule; an unfamiliar but transparently constructed word need not be meaningless. This reference uses pedagogically useful segmentation and marks historical claims only when they have source support. [[un + helpful] + ness] The outer suffix relates to the whole adjective unhelpful, not independently to help. derived stem + plural inflection Teachers is analysed as teacher plus plural marking, rather than teach plus an arbitrary ers suffix. Several helpful volunteers arrived. Helpful is an adjective related to help by derivation; volunteers carries ordinary plural inflection. The volunteers’ helpfulness reassured the organiser. Helpfulness is an abstract noun derived from an adjective; its noun status differs from the adjective’s modifier function. The editor questioned the new term’s usefulness, not its intelligibility. A coinage can be understandable while its suitability for a particular audience remains a separate editorial question. a frequent established word a productive word-building pattern Frequency concerns how often an expression occurs; productivity concerns extension of a pattern. Neither measure automatically entails the other. Plural allomorphs are not three different meanings of plurality. Pronunciation conditions the regular variants. Some apparent affixes are opaque or historically reanalysed; a synchronic analysis should not pretend every spelling can be cleanly segmented. Teachers contains only one morpheme because it is one written word. Teachers can be analysed as teach + -er + plural -s. A written word can contain several meaningful grammatical or lexical parts. A productive suffix can attach to any English word. Productive affixes still have category, meaning and other selection restrictions. Productivity is not unrestricted combination. allomorph A variant realisation of one morpheme. The regular plural has different sounds in cats and dogs. productivity The capacity of a pattern to extend to additional suitable forms. A speaker can use a familiar noun in a newly motivated verb use. base A form to which a morphological operation applies. Unhelpful is the base for -ness in unhelpfulness. source-de22cd3f568f72 source-6121c7a85de23d source-5d44e2f0f7c24c source-abb4eb7aa69725
